content: Single Whip (單鞭, dān biān) is a fundamental posture commonly found in various styles of Tai Chi Chuan. At the conclusion of this posture, the left hand is typically extended outward in a palm push, while the right hand is most often positioned in the form of a hook or a closed fist. However, notable exceptions include the Single Whip in Sun style and Wu/Hao style Tai Chi Chuan, where the posture concludes with both hands open and palms facing outward. This posture is one of the most frequently repeated movements in solo training forms. Its initial appearance in most forms occurs following the Grasp Sparrow's Tail sequence, which includes the movements peng, lu, ji, and an. Later in the sequence, it reappears as a variation known as Snake Creeps Down. Additionally, in the Wu style sword form, there exists a posture called Single Whip Fusing Throat. The martial applications of Single Whip are extensive and diverse. These include various strikes, throws, and change-ups, where one hand is used to create an opening for the other to strike. Furthermore, kicks and other techniques derived from this posture are practiced across different schools of Tai Chi Chuan.
